name: Monk Divine Dragon Monk
body:
A divine dragon monk venerates and emulates the five dragons that embody the five elements.

Sense the Soul (Sp)

At 1st level, a divine dragon monk can cast detect evil and detect magic at will as spell-like abilities using their class level as the caster level. This ability replaces the bonus feat granted at 1st level.

Smite Evil (Su)

At 1st level, a divine dragon monk gains smite evil as a paladin of their class level. This ability replaces flurry of blows.

Touch of the Fire Dragon (Su)

At 1st level, a divine dragon monk can cause their unarmed strikes to burst into flame. As a swift action, they can deal an additional 1d4 fire damage per 2 class levels on their next unarmed strike. A divine dragon monk can use this ability a number of times equal to their Wisdom modifier. This ability replaces stunning fist.

Scales of the Metal Dragon (Ex)

At 2nd level, a divine dragon monk has divinely inspired resilience.

Anytime they succeed on a spell effect that would impose a partial or half effect on a Fortitude or Will save, they instead are unaffected. This ability replaces evasion and improved evasion.

Resilience of the Earth Dragon (Ex)

At 5th level, a divine dragon monk is immune to stunning and sleep and effects that impose slow. This ability replaces purity of body.

Purity of the Water Dragon (Su)

At 11th level, a divine dragon monk, regains 1 hit point per hour.

Additionally, they can make a Fortitude save once per hour to recover ability score damage as if resting for 24 hours. The DC for the Fortitude save is 10 plus the ability score to be healed minus the total damage to the ability score. This ability replaces diamond body for the monk. The unchained monk gains this ability at 12th level and it replaces the ki power gained at that level.

Blending of the Wood Dragon (Sp)

At 15th level, a divine dragon monk can cast greater invisibility a number of times per day equal to their Wisdom modifier. The caster level for this effect is their class level. This ability replaces quivering palm for the monk or all style strikes for the unchained monk.
